text:
Alyssa: Heads up — ACME reported a p99 jump (~800ms extra) on hosted inference starting ~03:10 UTC after yesterday's continuous-batcher config deploy. Seems correlated with the change that bumped max_batch_size -> 64 and reduced hold_timeout -> 5ms. Any eyeballs? Link to quick graphs: https://grafana.redwood/acme/p99

Jordan: Yep, I saw a cluster-wide p99 increase from ~220ms to ~1.1s around that time. Traffic shift: a lot more tiny requests (<=8 tokens). With max_batch_size high and low hold timeout, we're getting occasional long waits when arrival jitter is low.

Sam: Customer repro notes: run 5 concurrent tiny prompts, loop 1000x, they see ~12% responses >900ms. They'll share the exact prompt set.

Maria: Customer is blocked — this affects their live-chat SLA. They asked for an urgent mitigation and ETA.

Jordan: Initial root cause hypothesis: greedy batch sizing + reduced timeout = more head-of-line queuing for tiny requests. Also noticed coalescer backpressure when CPU spikes which increases queuing latency for some batches.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary-change-requested by Jordan — applying canary config to pool-a (2 nodes).

Alyssa: Proposed mitigations (short term):
  1) Rollback max_batch_size to 16 for affected pool(s)
  2) Switch tiny-prompt route to time-first (prefer low hold time) instead of size-first batching
  3) Add fast-path flush: if batch size <8 but observed p95/p99 rising, flush immediately
  4) Increase scheduling priority for tiny requests to reduce head-of-line blocking

Jordan: Rollback dry-run command I used: `redwoodctl configs set continuous_batcher.pool=pool-a max_batch_size=16 --dry-run`
Logs I looked at: `tail -n 200 /var/log/batcher.log | grep hold_timeout` shows occasional full-timeout waits instead of early flush.

Sam: Can you paste the repro script so we can run against the customer's tenant?

Jordan: Repro script (tiny prompts, quick):
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"Hi"}' &
  sleep 0.05
done
wait
```
Run with 5 parallel shells to mimic customer concurrency.

Maria: Customer ran the canary on their side (we asked to hit only the canary nodes) — p99 dropped from ~1.12s to ~0.27s on those nodes. They want a full rollback.

Alyssa: I'll schedule a rollback of the config for pool-a in 10 minutes after monitoring baseline. Also adding a short-term alert: `ALERT if p99(tiny-prompt-route) > 600ms for 5m` to catch regressions during rollback.

Jordan: Postmortem action items: add regression test for tiny prompts vs batching configs; implement auto-suggestion in optimizer to cap max_batch_size based on median token length and request-size histogram; and add metric to detect hold-time-full events.

Sam: I'll keep ACME updated and share status. Thanks for the quick canary. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: metric-summary: tiny-prompt-route p99 BEFORE=1.12s AFTER-canary=0.27s. Canary nodes healthy 2/2.

Alyssa: Thanks everyone. Filing ticket INF-4721 with remediation steps and timeline, will escalate to on-call if rollback doesn't stabilize p99 within 15m.

Jordan: FYI — if rollback isn't enough, next step is to enable tiny-request fast-path rollout cluster-wide and an emergency config that forces immediate flush when token_count <= 8.

Sam: Noted. I'll add customer-facing wording for the incident and ETA.

Maria: Customer acknowledged temporary rollback OK, asks for follow-up postmortem and config guardrails.

Alyssa: Noted — I'll add root-cause + mitigation + follow-ups to the ticket. Closing here after rollback completes and metrics stabilize.
